confidentUnsupported.evidence: 'That inconsistent light cycle is a classic sign of a mechanical thermostat that has lost its calibration' and 'call an engineer to fit the new thermostat safely' without any temperature measurement, preheat or seal check

unjustifiedPart.evidence: 'you've confirmed the thermostat is faulty and needs replacing' / 'fit the new thermostat' despite the customer having no thermometer and no readings taken

rationale: The assistant correctly identified a mechanical-thermostat cooker from the dials/neon description and kept instructions safe (look through glass only, engineer for internal wiring). However it never asked about preheating, shelf position or the door seal, never suggested buying a cheap oven thermometer after the customer said she had none, and the third reply references a thermometer check it never actually set up. It then declared the neon pattern a 'classic sign' of a failed thermostat and told the customer to have an engineer fit a new one, a confident part replacement the ground truth says is only justified after temperature measurements.
